week_headline: Vitamin D is dominating health conversations this week, with millions questioning whether their supplement is actually the right form

claims.verdict: D3 does appear to raise blood levels of vitamin D more effectively than D2 in most studies, and it sticks around in the body longer — so on balance, D3 is the better pick for most people. That said, D2 still works, is widely used in fortified foods, and is the preferred option for vegans since D3 is typically derived from lanolin in sheep's wool. The gap between them is real but often overstated — both beat doing nothing if you're deficient.
claims.verdict_highlight: D3 raises levels better, but D2 still works
sources: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition (Tripkovic et al., 2017 — D3 vs D2 meta-analysis)

claims.global_opinion: In the UK and much of Europe, D2 has historically dominated food fortification programmes and prescription supplements, so many Europeans have been getting D2 for years without issue. The US has shifted more toward D3 in over-the-counter products, reflecting the growing evidence of its superior bioavailability. In parts of South Asia and the Middle East, vitamin D deficiency is widespread despite sun exposure, and local health bodies are increasingly recommending D3 supplementation regardless of form debates.
claims.brit_take: Half the UK is quietly deficient from October to March anyway, so arguing about which form to take is a lovely problem to have — just take one of them, preferably with your toast.
